column1: esteem§Self-esteem built on one result is fragile.§建立在单一成绩上的**自尊**很脆弱。
estrangement§The estrangement began over money and continued over nothing.§这场**疏远**因钱而起，后来则毫无缘由地延续下去。
ethical§An ethical code that fits on a card is worth reading twice.§一份能写在卡片上的**道德准则**值得读两遍。
eulogize§He eulogized the building on the day it was demolished.§大楼被拆的那天，他为它写下**颂词**。
eulogy§She wrote her own eulogy and asked that it be read plainly.§她自己写好了**悼词**，要求平实地读出来。
euphemism§Every profession invents a euphemism for failure.§每个行业都为失败发明一个**委婉的说法**。
euphonious§He chose the more euphonious of two accurate translations.§在两个同样准确的译法中，他选了更**悦耳**的那个。
euphoric§The euphoric first week of any project is the least productive.§任何项目**欣快的**第一周，都是产出最少的一周。
evade§Water evades every barrier that is not continuous.§水会**绕过**任何不连续的屏障。
evaluation§Evaluation of the pilot took longer than the pilot itself.§对试点的**评估**比试点本身还久。
evanescent§Evanescent as it is, the effect can be photographed.§这种效应虽**转瞬即逝**，却能被拍下来。
evenhanded§An evenhanded account satisfies neither side, which is a good sign.§**不偏不倚**的叙述让双方都不满意，这是个好迹象。
eventuality§In the event of that eventuality, the fund covers six months.§一旦发生**那种情况**，这笔基金可支撑半年。
everlasting§Nothing here is everlasting except the argument about the roof.§这里没有什么是**永恒的**，除了关于屋顶的争论。
evolve§The word evolved from a term of abuse into a compliment.§这个词从骂人话**演变**成了赞美。
exacerbate§Explaining a joke exacerbates the silence.§解释笑话只会让冷场**更尴尬**。
exaggerate§She never exaggerates, which makes her superlatives count.§她从不**夸张**，所以她的最高级很有分量。
exaggeration§It is no exaggeration to say the index took longer than the text.§说索引比正文花的时间还长，并不**夸张**。
exalt§Do not exalt one method into a doctrine.§不要把一种方法**抬高成教条**。
exasperation§Exasperation is the emotion most likely to end up in print.§**恼怒**是最容易被写进文字的情绪。
excavate§They excavated the drain and found the missing wall.§他们**挖开**排水沟，找到了那道消失的墙。
excessive§Excessive detail in a summary defeats its purpose.§摘要里细节**过多**就失去了意义。
excise§Excise duty on salt shaped two centuries of smuggling.§盐的**消费税**塑造了两个世纪的走私。
excitement§The excitement of a new archive lasts about four days.§新档案带来的**兴奋**大约持续四天。
exclude§Excluding the outliers changes the conclusion, which is the problem.§**剔除**异常值会改变结论，问题正在于此。
exclusive§The interview was exclusive and told us nothing new.§这次专访是**独家**的，却没告诉我们任何新东西。
excursion§An excursion into the footnotes rewarded the patient reader.§深入脚注的一番**游历**回报了耐心的读者。
execution§The execution of the plan fell to people who had not written it.§**执行**这个计划的落到了没参与制定它的人头上。
exemplary§The archive is exemplary in one respect: everything is labeled.§这座档案馆在一点上**堪称典范**：什么都贴了标签。
exempt§Nobody is exempt from proofreading, including the editor.§谁都不能**免于**校对，编辑也不例外。
exhaustive§An exhaustive list is rarely a useful one.§**穷尽式**的清单很少有用。
exhibit§The letters are Exhibit C and settled the case.§这些信件是**证物**三，决定了案子的结果。
exhilarate§Getting the method right exhilarates more than getting the answer.§把方法弄对比得出答案更让人**振奋**。
exorbitant§Exorbitant rents emptied the street of everything but banks.§**高得离谱**的租金让这条街上只剩下银行。
exotic§What is exotic here is ordinary two valleys away.§这里的**异国**情调，隔两个山谷就是寻常。
expansion§Thermal expansion cracked the pipe in the first cold week.§第一个寒冷的星期，**热胀**就把管子撑裂了。
expansive§He grew expansive after the second cup and told us everything.§第二杯之后他变得**健谈**，把一切都说了。
expediency§Expediency now, principle later, is how most rules get written.§先讲**权宜**、后谈原则，多数规则就是这么写出来的。
expedient§It seemed expedient at the time and looks shabby now.§这在当时似乎是**权宜之计**，如今看来很不体面。
expedite§Nothing expedites a decision like a visible deadline.§没有什么比一个看得见的截止日期更能**加快**决策。
expeditious§An expeditious reply is worth more than a thorough late one.§**迅速的**回复胜过详尽但迟到的回复。
expendable§Treating a step as expendable is how the fault got through.§把某个步骤当作**可省略**的，故障就是这么溜过去的。
experimental§Experimental music of the period is now background in adverts.§那个时期的**实验**音乐，如今成了广告的背景音。
experimentation§Experimentation stops when the funding is annual.§资助按年发放时，**实验**就停下来了。
expertise§Expertise is knowing which of the rules can be broken.§**专业能力**，就是知道哪些规则可以打破。
explanatory§An explanatory diagram beats three explanatory paragraphs.§一张**说明**图胜过三段说明文字。
explosive§The mixture is explosive only above a certain temperature.§这种混合物只有超过某个温度才会**爆炸**。
expropriate§The council expropriated a strip six metres wide.§议会**征用**了一条六米宽的地带。
expropriation§Expropriation of the mills ended a family business of two centuries.§磨坊被**征收**，终结了一个两百年的家族生意。
expurgate§The expurgated edition sold twice as well as the complete one.§**删节版**的销量是全本的两倍。
extant§The earliest extant photograph of the street dates from 1867.§这条街**现存**最早的照片摄于一八六七年。
extemporaneous§An extemporaneous answer reveals what the prepared one hides.§**即席的**回答会暴露准备好的答案所掩盖的东西。
extend§He extended a hand and the argument was over.§他**伸出**手，争论就结束了。
extensive§Extensive damage was found behind a wall nobody had opened.§在一堵从未打开过的墙后发现了**大面积**损坏。
extenuate§Circumstances may extenuate the delay but not the silence.§**情有可原**的是延误，而不是沉默。
external§An external examiner reads what the department cannot see.§**校外**考官读得出这个系自己看不见的东西。
extinct§The dialect is not extinct; it has eleven speakers.§这种方言并未**消亡**，还有十一个人在说。
extinction§Extinction of the local variety went unrecorded for decades.§当地品种的**灭绝**几十年来无人记录。
extol§To extol a method is not to have tested it.§**称颂**一种方法不等于检验过它。
extract§The dentist extracted the tooth and kept talking.§牙医**拔了牙**，嘴上还在说个不停。
extraneous§Extraneous light ruined three of the four exposures.§**杂散光**毁了四次曝光中的三次。
extravagance§The one extravagance in the house was the staircase.§这栋房子里唯一的**奢侈**之处是楼梯。
extravagant§Extravagant claims are easy to make and hard to withdraw.§**夸张**的说法容易提出，难以收回。
extremist§No extremist ever describes himself as one.§没有哪个**极端主义者**会这样称呼自己。
